transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Recording: Fireflies.ai export
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Delgado (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Security PM); Daniel Park (Helix Head of IT), Sasha Ivanov (Helix Compliance), Mina Alvarez (Helix GRC)

Summary (auto): High-level SOC 2 / ISO27001 posture walk through. Customer requested specific evidence for six controls and asked about mechanisms for encrypted keys, RBAC, SSO integration (SAML), audit logs retention and secure transfer of artifacts. Agreed next steps: Redwood to upload reports & certs to secure link, SE to prepare KMS integration notes, schedule hands-on evidence handoff.

00:00:02 Alyssa Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we'll go through our SOC 2 and ISO posture, then map the Helix control list to the artifacts we can provide.
00:00:17 Daniel Park: Thanks, Alyssa. Quick context first — we're building an internal LLM-assisted triage for clinical notes, so PHI sensitivity is a thing. We need the compliance story to line up.
00:00:30 Marco Delgado: Understood. We treat Private + Dedicated differently; for PHI-heavy workloads we recommend private or dedicated with customer-managed keys. We'll cover encryption and KMS in detail.
00:00:45 Sasha Ivanov: On the controls list, our audit team specifically asked for RBAC evidence, SSO/SAML configuration, rotation of keys, and audit logs retention up to 7 years for certain datasets. Can Redwood provide mapping to SOC controls for each?
00:01:04 Priya Nair: Yes, we have a controls mapping matrix. We'll send a CSV that maps Redwood policy and artifacts to Helix control IDs. Today we can walk the high-level and flag anything that needs a new artifact.
00:01:20 Mina Alvarez: Also need to confirm data residency options — EU vs US — and whether logs can be retained regionally.

00:05:12 Marco Delgado: Quick note on terminology — our product names sometimes get munged in transcriptions, so when I say 'Redwood Private' I'm meaning the VPC/on-prem package; 'Dedicated' is reserved GPU pools. For KMS we integrate with AWS KMS and also support customer HSMs via bring-your-own-key APIs.
00:05:46 Daniel Park: How do you surface proof of key custody — like do you provide attestation for KMS rotations?
00:06:03 Marco Delgado: We provide rotation logs and we can show KMS CMK ARNs and rotation policies; we also export key usage audit events into the audit log stream that's part of the trust artifacts. There is a caveat: we don't hold your plaintext keys in Redwood. If you use BYOK/HSM we never see private key material.
00:06:30 Sasha Ivanov: That's good. How about SSO — our SAML provider is Okta and we need SCIM provisioning evidence and RBAC mappings down to role IDs.
00:06:47 Priya Nair: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM user provisioning. The artifacts we can provide: SAML metadata exchange logs, SCIM provisioning event records, RBAC export (role -> permission) snapshots, and sample Admin audit trails showing changes. The RBAC export is CSV; we can redact user GUIDs if needed.
00:07:12 Daniel Park: Can logs be pushed to our SIEM (Splunk) or do we pull from an S3 bucket?
00:07:25 Marco Delgado: Both. We have an event streaming option (Kafka/http) to push, and we also drop raw event batches into a customer-owned S3. For compliance we typically provision a read-only S3 bucket and an agreed retention lifecycle.
00:07:42 Mina Alvarez: Retention lifecycle — do you support custom object lifecycle policies by region? We need EU logs to remain in eu-west-1 for residency.
00:08:00 Marco Delgado: Yes, you can pin region on Private or Dedicated. On Hosted we offer region selection and logs can be routed to region-bound S3. We'll detail that in the artifacts pack.

00:12:10 Sasha Ivanov: About the SOC 2 — do you have a Type II for the previous 12 months? We need the testing period documented.
00:12:21 Alyssa Chen: We do. I'll share the redacted SOC 2 Type II report. It covers the period 2024-09 through 2025-03; our auditor is ClearStream (third party). ISO 27001 cert is current and I will include the scope document.
00:12:38 Daniel Park: Will that include the list of in-scope systems? We need to confirm whether the inference runtime is in-scope for ISO.
00:12:50 Priya Nair: The ISO scope lists the inference runtime, control plane, and telemetry processing. We'll attach the scope statement in the cert bundle. Some names in the scope map to internal service names (ex: "inference-svc"), that might require a dab of translation but we'll provide a mapping file.

00:18:05 Mina Alvarez: On audit logs, we need immutable logs for certain control objectives. How do you guarantee immutability?
00:18:18 Marco Delgado: We use write-once S3 with object lock option for archived evidence, and for active streams we sign events and store a hash ledger. There's an internal integrity process and we can export signed digests. (note: wording sometimes shows up as "sign ledgers" in logs).
00:18:40 Sasha Ivanov: We'll want a short doc describing the digest format and verification steps so our auditors can validate.
00:18:55 Marco Delgado: We'll include that.

00:24:22 Daniel Park: Encryption in transit and at rest — specifics please. Our legal wants to see TLS termination points and whether plaintext crosses Redwood infra.
00:24:36 Priya Nair: TLS is end-to-end — we terminate at customer-chosen ingress for Private deployments. For Hosted with cross-region we terminate at our edge and re-encrypt to backend. We will provide network diagrams showing termination points and where plaintext is never persisted. I'll add that to the evidence pack.

00:29:10 Sasha Ivanov: On key rotation, do you support automatic rotation cadence? We need proof that keys are rotated every 90 days or according to policy.
00:29:25 Marco Delgado: We can show rotation schedules and rotation logs. For AWS KMS we can show the CMK rotation bit and rotation events. For HSM/BYOK, rotation is customer-driven but we capture rotation events in the audit stream.

00:33:02 Mina Alvarez: A couple of nitty-gritty asks: can you provide sample policy configs for RBAC and a demo account that shows role elevation and approval flows? Our auditors like to see the workflow.
00:33:18 Alyssa Chen: Yes, we can set up a short demo tenant or provide recorded screencap showing role elevation. We'll coordinate offline on tenant provisioning.

00:38:40 Daniel Park: About control mapping — we want to map Redwood artifacts to our control IDs. How granular is your mapping?
00:38:54 Priya Nair: We maintain a controls matrix that maps to common frameworks — SOC 2 CC, ISO Annex A, and a generic NIST mapping. For your project we'll map each Helix control ID to the specific artifact: log export, policy doc, config screenshot, or attestation letter.
00:39:20 Sasha Ivanov: Any gaps we should know about up front?
00:39:29 Priya Nair: One area that sometimes needs custom evidence is vendor management for third-party model providers if you're using external LLM weights. If your workflow pulls models from public registries, we can provide procurement attestations but not internal vendor security reviews for those external model authors.
00:39:50 Daniel Park: We're planning to use Redwood-curated open models, not external closed vendors. But we may want to run an approved-list process.

00:44:00 Marco Delgado: Quick technical caveat — when we say "KV cache" in some docs, it's a short-hand for our key-value reuse cache. That is client-side request caching and doesn't hold PII beyond ephemeral session keys. Transcription may show weird phrases; sorry for the noise.
00:44:19 Mina Alvarez: Good to call out. We'll still want to know retention on caches and whether they can be disabled for sensitive endpoints.
00:44:32 Marco Delgado: Caches can be disabled per-route. We'll show config snippets.

00:50:05 Alyssa Chen: Recap of next steps: Redwood will provision a gated S3 link with the redacted SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert; SE (Marco) will upload KMS integration notes and the audit digest verification doc; we'll send the controls mapping CSV and schedule the handoff session for the week of Oct 27. Anything to add?
00:50:30 Sasha Ivanov: Please include sample RBAC export and SCIM provisioning events. Also please label any artifacts that are redacted and note why redaction was done.
00:50:44 Alyssa Chen: Will do.
00:52:10 Daniel Park: On timeline, we aim to complete our internal assessment by mid-November so we may start pilot in Dec. Is that feasible?
00:52:25 Priya Nair: Yes, that timeline aligns. The evidence handoff and a short POC for Private/Dedicated switching would fit.
00:52:38 Mina Alvarez: One last ask — can we get a short statement of responsibility for data residency vs customer responsibility? Our legal wants the delineation in writing.
00:52:53 Alyssa Chen: We'll include a one-page responsibility matrix (Redwood vs Helix) with the artifacts.
00:53:10 Marco Delgado: Also note: for Private on-prem installs we hand over full control plane and key custody is customer-only.
00:53:25 Sasha Ivanov: Great. Thanks team.
00:57:55 Alyssa Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifact link and calendar invite for the evidence handoff.
